title: policy-evaluator-priority-inversion-causing-temporary-undercharge-and-silent-allow
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: The policy evaluator sometimes selects a lower‑restrictiveness policy when merging per-key, per-org and per-route rules during rapid rollout/config changes. This leads to silent allows: requests are not throttled as expected and corresponding metering/billing increments are undercounted for a short window (typically ~5–20s in production). Impact: affects high‑throughput tenants using route aliases and streaming responses; results in underbilling and potential SLO violations for quota enforcement. Root cause hypothesis: the comparator used to pick the "winning" policy when multiple scopes apply uses a tie-breaker that combines numeric priority (higher = stricter) and a timestamp of policy last_update truncated to seconds. In high churn rollouts the truncated timestamp can be identical across rules, and an integer arithmetic path in the comparator can flip sign when a feature flag metadata is present (observed on 64->32 bit cast in the evaluation shim). Additionally, the evaluator caches the selected policy for the duration of the streaming session and later applies metering increments to that cached bucket; if the policy decision was inverted at session start and a stricter policy is later activated, the tokens emitted during the stream are not attributed to the stricter bucket. Repro steps: 1) Create two policies via admin API: per-key (priority 100, strict windowed debit) and per-org (priority 50, relaxed). 2) Rapidly update per-org policy metadata timestamp (via admin tool) to simulate rollout (<1s granularity). 3) Open a streaming generation request using API key tied to the per-key policy and a route alias (curl example provided below). 4) Observe that policy chosen is the per-org relaxed rule and token counters increment only on that bucket. curl example: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"open-text-16k","stream":true,"prompt":"...long prompt..."}' Logs to check: - rate-eval.log entries with evaluator.choice at DEBUG - meter-commit.log for token attribution - admin audit for policy updates Observed evidence: - DEBUG traces show comparator returning -1 when comparing per-key vs per-org in 8/12 reproductions. - Metering increments show tokens posted to per-org buckets while enforcer trace shows per-key SHOULD_HAVE_APPLIED. - Canary that toggles the feature flag which activates the 32-bit shim correlated with incidents. Temporary mitigation implemented: feature flag off for the evaluation shim (rollout revert), deploy a short-circuit enforcer patch that chooses the stricter of (cached_policy, current_evaluation) when policy precedence is ambiguous, and start a reconciliation job to detect and flag undercharged windows for manual review. Permanent plan: 1) Fix comparator logic in evaluator: use explicit 128-bit safe compare path and remove timestamp truncation (switch to nanosecond precision). 2) Remove caching of policy decision for the entire streaming session; instead, evaluate at stream start and stitch at chunk boundaries with a fallback to enforce stricter policy during conflicts. 3) Add unit tests covering priority inversion and a long‑running integration test that simulates concurrent policy updates + active streams. 4) Add an observability metric policy_inversion_count and dashboard alert for >1/min for any org. 5) Run a billing reconciliation job and customer outreach for affected tenants. Rollout plan: patch -> canary (small % of runtime nodes) -> expand after 24h with zero inversion observed -> full rollout with runtime-1.21. Owners: evaluator eng (Ethan Chen), billing reconciliation (Priya Nambiar), console notifications (Luca Rossi). Dependencies: ["ENG-312210","ENG-204001"]
